column3: Close to the Hebrew; “a relative” follows the reading tradition (Qere), while the written text means “an acquaintance”; “a man of great wealth” renders “a mighty man of valor (worth).”
Close to the Hebrew; the last clause is obscure in the Hebrew, and “though she rested a little in the house” is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “wings” is the same word as in 3:9.
Close to the Hebrew; “His kindness” may refer to the LORD or to Boaz, and “close relatives” renders “go'el,” the kinsman-redeemer.
